SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Dros.]
Clawing sensation in pit of stomach.
Contractive tension at pit of stomach, as if everything would be drawn inwards, especially during deep inhalation, and with cough.
   

HYPOCHONDRIA. [18] [Dros.]
Anxious feeling in the hypochondria.
Painful to touch, and when coughing.
Must support the hypochondria with the hands when coughing. θ Pertussis.
Constrictive pain in both hypochondria, impeding coughing ; unable to cough on account of pain, unless hand is pressed upon pit of stomach.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Dros.]
Painful constriction of epigastrium.
Dull stitch from right to left across abdomen, almost taking the breath, while walking.
Stitches in right side of abdomen while sitting.
Stitch from left loin into penis.
Constriction in abdomen, with vomiting. θ Pertussis.
Bellyache after sour food.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Dros.]
Outward pressing pain, independent of stool.
Frequent stool, with colic.
Stools : soft, fluid ; loose ; papescent ; white, slimy and stinking, with watery, odorless urine.
Loose stool almost continually, but rather < after midnight ; bloody, mucous or offensive stools, followed by pains in abdomen and small of back.
Before and after stool ; tensive pain in upper part of abdomen while holding breath.
After stool : ineffectual straining ; constant inclination to stool ; abdominal and dorsal pains.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Dros.]
Frequent urging to urinate, with scanty discharge, frequently only by drops.
Frequent, profuse urination.
Urine dark and of strong smell.
Urine watery, inodorous, with fetid mucous stool.
   

MALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [22] [Dros.]
Drawing stitches from left loin into penis.
Itching stitches in the glans penis.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Dros.]
Delay of the first menses.
Menses too late ; too scanty ; suppression of menses ; blood dark.
Leucorrhœa, with labor-like pain.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Dros.]
Voice : hoarse, deep, requires exertion to speak ; husky ; hollow, toneless ; cracked.
Catarrhal hoarseness, with or without coryza or cough ; is only able to speak in a bass voice ; hoarseness after measles.
Chronic persistent hoarseness resulting from repeated catarrhal attacks.
Great hoarseness, with spasmodic cough, after measles.
Epiglottis in constant motion to and fro, constant endeavor to cough ; larynx very dry ; patient involuntarily supports thyroid cartilage on swallowing or coughing, and there appears to be a constant strain in box of larynx, with disposition to vomit. θ Laryngitis.
Constant tickling in larynx, causing cough and preventing sleep at night.
Sensation like from a feather in larynx, exciting cough.
Crawling in larynx, which provokes hacking cough, with sensation as if a soft substance were in it, with fine stitches extending thence to right side of pharynx.
Bruised feeling in larynx whilst inhaling.
Constriction of the larynx when talking.
Mucus in the larynx, either hard or soft.
Chest and throat symptoms worse from talking or singing.
Laryngeal phthisis, with hoarseness, rapid emaciation.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Dros.]
Oppression, with every word he speaks the throat contracts ; not so when walking.
Respiration slow ; predominant with moist sound.
Intolerable stitches when coughing and taking a deep inspiration, in the upper part of the chest near the axilla, > by pressing on affected part with the hand, with purulent expectoration mixed with blood.
Whilst inhaling, felt severe aching pains in and below both clavicles, over a small space in lungs ; the infra-clavicular pain afterwards extended round to the scapulæ ; also a bruised feeling of the larynx.
Sensation as if something in chest prevented exhalation when talking or coughing.
Oppressive sensation in chest as if expiration were prevented by coughing or talking.
During an expiration in evening, when lying in bed, sudden contraction of abdomen occasioning a heaving as if he would vomit and bringing on cough.
Difficult breathing, < after midnight.
Dyspnœa, especially on talking, with every word throat becomes constricted ; no dyspnœa while walking.
Severe dyspnœa threatening suffocation ; blueness of face and lips ; cold sweat on forehead ; vomiting of tough mucus. θ Whooping cough.
Oppression of chest as if from holding back the breath.
Attack of suffocation ; cannot recover the breath ; gasping.
Asthma, particularly when talking, with contraction of throat at every word that is uttered.
Bad, offensive-smelling breath when coughing.
   

COUGH. [27] [Dros.]
Deep sounding, hoarse barking cough.
Rough, scraping, dry sensation deep in fauces and soft palate, causing hacking cough, with yellow mucous expectoration and hoarseness, speaks only with exertion, and in a deep bass voice ; oppression of chest as if air was withheld on talking and coughing, so that breath could not be expired.
Whooping cough ; attacks, every one to three hours, with barking or dull-sounding coughs, choking breathing, caused by tickling or dryness in throat, or from a sensation of a soft feather in larynx ; expectoration, only in morning, yellow and bitter ; has to swallow the mucus.
Attacks of coughing preceded, fifteen or twenty minutes, by rattling of mucus in bronchial tubes to which patient solely ascribes attack of coughing. θ Whooping cough.
Whooping cough, with feeling of constriction in chest and hypochondria, so that patient tries to support these parts with hands ; < after midnight ; perspires on waking from sleep.
Cough comes in fits, at long intervals ; cough during intervals is short, not exhausting, and he considers it trifling in comparison with the tormenting attacks ; the fits begin mildly, are short, but increase during course of disease, until cough becomes unceasing, the attacks occur in quick succession, and forces to sit up, always beginning with titillation and renewed inspiration, until finally vomiting of mucus (rarely of food) sets in, which finishes the paroxysm ; great exhaustion after the fit ; frequently < at night on lying down. θ Whooping cough.
Paroxysmal dry cough, exciting cause of which seems to be in abdomen with copious perspiration over whole body and culminating in an attack of severe nausea.
Spasmodic, nervous, and sympathetic cough.
Spasmodic cough of phthisical girls.
When coughing a feeling as if something kept the air in the chest, cannot cough right, cannot speak.
Whooping cough, with hemorrhage from mouth and nose, anguish, blue face, wheezing breathing, suffocation.
During cough : face pale or bluish ; efforts to vomit ; vomiting of water, mucus and food ; stitches in muscles of chest ; bleeding from nose or mouth ; has to support chest and hypochondria ; hoarseness ; offensive breath ; rising up in bed with fear and trembling.
Attacks characterized by certain typhoid conditions, with severe spasmodic retraction of abdomen, followed by vomiting of food, mucus and water. θ Whooping cough.
Cough which marks the sequela of measles, especially when it occurs in paroxysms, and is < in afternoon and evening ; even when cough is attended by bloody and purulent expectoration.
Very hoarse cough, < after midnight, during or after measles.
Spasmodic cough, attended by retching and vomiting.
Cough when singing, causing smarting in larynx.
Harassing, titillating cough in children, not at all during day, but commences as soon as head touches pillow at night.
Cough, in evening, immediately after lying down.
The fever and cough, which is very hoarse, are worse after twelve at night. θ Bronchitis infantum.
Awakes at night about 2 o'clock, coughs for a short time and then falls asleep again.
Nocturnal cough of phthisical patients.
Severe cough of young phthisical subjects, with bloody and purulent expectoration.
Cough sounds loose, nothing comes up. θ Catarrh.
Cough, with expectoration of bright red frothy or of black clotted blood.
Bloody and purulent expectoration after measles.
Very violent cough ; spitting of blood and pus, with violent pains in chest. θ Phthisis.
Expectoration : yellow ; bitter ; offensive ; bloody ; pus-like ; salty ; has to be swallowed.
Cough aggravated : by warmth ; drinking ; tobacco smoke ; laughing ; singing ; weeping ; after lying down ; after midnight or in the morning.
   

INNER CHEST AND LUNGS. [28] [Dros.]
Constriction of chest and hypochondria.
Cough with sense of constriction in chest, which seems to hold breath back and prevent coughing, with pain in ribs, so that he is compelled to support the parts with hands ; vomiting of food, then of mucus and water.
Tightness of chest, especially when talking, or even uttering a single word ; > while walking ; the throat seems to contract.
Severe stitches in chest when sneezing or coughing, must press on chest with hands, for relief.
Violent oppressive stitching pain across chest, passing off during motion.
Sensation of oppression in chest as if the air were retained when coughing, and as if breath could not be expelled.
Burning sensation in centre of chest.
Bronchitis of old age, in connection with emphysema or Bronchiectasis ; nocturnal paroxysms ; < lying down ; cough seems to come from abdomen, shaking all the muscles of chest and body, with much exhaustion after attack ; expectoration of yellow mucus or pus ; paroxysms of cough from one to two hours apart.
Phthisis with severe pains in chest, purulent expectoration and foul pus-like taste in mouth.
Tuberculosis.
   

OUTER CHEST. [30] [Dros.]
Stitches in muscles of chest, when breathing or coughing.
Sternum painful when pressing on it, as from festering under skin.
Black pores on chest and shoulder.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Dros.]
Neck and Back
Neck still and painful on motion.
Nape of neck painful to touch.
Pain between scapulæ drawing to small of back.
Stitching tearing from spine to anterior spinous process of left ilium, when sitting.
Back pains as if bruised, in the morning.
Itching stitch in coccyx when sitting.
   

UPPER LIMBS. [32] [Dros.]
Quivering on right shoulder when at rest.
Nightly pains in humerus, going off by day during motion.
Coldness of the hands.
Deep ulcer on back of right hand discharging bloody water.
Red spots on back of hand and behind wrist.
Fingers spasmodically contracted, rigid in grasping.
